title: Modric 'ashamed' of Croatia's heaviest-ever loss to England
subtitle: England's attackers ran riot in a 7-0 victory over Croatia, leaving experienced midfielder Luka Modric furious.
paragraphs: Luka Modric said Croatia's historic 7-0 defeat to England in the Nations League represented the first time he had felt "ashamed" in his illustrious international career.
Croatia slumped to the heaviest loss in their history on Saturday, in front of a crowd mostly made up of schoolchildren in Rijeka, due to UEFA-enforced restrictions on the home side.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Bukayo Saka all scored before half-time, marking the first time England had seen four different players get on the scoresheet before the interval since March 2013 against San Marino (Frank Lampard, Jermain Defoe, Ashley Young, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain).
Kane and Saka then got another goal apiece as Thomas Tuchel's side refused to ease up after the break, while Morgan Rogers came off the bench to score England's seventh.

Croatia had never previously lost a home game by more than a three-goal margin, going down 4-1 to the same opponents in September 2008, while a 6-0 loss in Spain in 2018 was their previous worst-ever defeat.
And the scoreline was no fluke, either, with England putting up a huge expected goals (xG) figure of 6.43 to Croatia's 1.39.
That is the largest figure ever amassed by any team in a Nations League game by some distance, surpassing Belarus' 4.89 xG against San Marino in September 2018.
And Modric did not mince his words concerning Croatia's display after full-time, saying: "You can't play football like that. We looked like we had four or five less players.
"It is difficult to find an explanation for such a performance, without winning duels, making fouls, showing aggressiveness and togetherness.
"I've been here for 20 years, but for the first time, I feel ashamed after a game.
"You can lose, or you can play against an opponent who is better – and they are right now.
"But losing like this and squandering the reputation we've built over the years is unacceptable. I feel ashamed."

Things do not get any easier for Croatia, either, as they host Spain in their final game of this international break on Tuesday, knowing a defeat would almost certainly end their chances of qualifying for the last eight.
"We need to come together and stay united because another difficult game awaits us," Modric added.
"We have to show our true selves, that we have fight and pride, desire, willpower and unity. You can't lose that overnight."
Head coach Slaven Bilic, meanwhile, was at a loss to explain Croatia's complete loss of organisation.
"It is difficult to say anything after a night like this. We are sad, disappointed, and I feel sorry for the fans and the children who were at the game," Bilic said.
"We talked, it is hardest for us, and we did not expect this would happen. I don't know what to call it, whether it's a blackout, but it's hard to analyse a game when you lose 7-0.
"We knew they were a top team, but that we couldn't match them in any way... that attacks your confidence, your will, and everything falls apart and goes the wrong way."
